application.product: TinyTranslator — a browser-only editor for Angular i18n translation files (XLIFF 1.2, XLIFF 2.0, XMB/XTB)
application.frontend: Angular 5 single-page application generated by Angular CLI 1.x, hash routing, Angular Material
application.backend: none. There is no server source in this repository; persistence is browser localStorage. The Dockerfile builds an nginx image that serves the already-built dist/ as static files.
application.persistence: localStorage, through a single BackendLocalStorageService behind BackendServiceAPI. No IndexedDB anywhere in the tree.
application.fleetShape: 56 stars, 9 forks, 25 open issues at acquisition — a weak fleet shape, recorded as a fact. This cell was cut for its workspace format, not for popularity.

legacyCell.declaredNote: The repository states no Node version anywhere: no engines block, no .nvmrc, no CI configuration, and a README that says only `install npm or (if you prefer it) yarn`. The only constraint reachable from the pin is @angular/cli 1.5.4's own engines block, node >= 6.9.0.
legacyCell.workspaceFormat: .angular-cli.json — the pre-angular.json Angular CLI workspace format, with a single apps[] entry, environmentSource plus a named environments map, styleExt, and a top-level e2e.protractor.config. This is the capability the fixture exists to carry.
legacyCell.bundler: webpack 3.8.1, supplied by @angular/cli 1.5.4 and not directly declared by the repository

node.platform: darwin-x64 executed on darwin-arm64 through Rosetta 2
node.honestLabel: era-declared, not repository-pinned. Node 8.9.3 was the active LTS two days before the pinned commit and satisfies the CLI's >= 6.9.0 floor. The workspace already held a Rosetta x64 Node 12.14.1 and a native arm64 Node 16.20.2 from earlier ingests; both are outside the Angular CLI 1.5 era band, so neither was used and the era runtime was acquired instead. That is a labeled deviation from the host defaults, made deliberately rather than by convenience.

packageManager.why: the repository commits a yarn.lock; npm would ignore it and resolve the ranges fresh, discarding the pin that makes this fixture reproducible
packageManager.eraContemporary: released 2017-11-28, ten days before the pinned commit

legacyCell.lifecycleScripts: enabled — node-sass 4.5.3 is a required build input and resolved a prebuilt darwin-x64-57 binding

buildCommands.repositoryOwnProduction: yarn run build-prod-en (one locale of the four-locale build-prod chain)

legacyCell.rationale: There is no declared cell to honour, so the cell was declared by era: the LTS runtime contemporary with the tag, the package manager the committed lockfile implies, and a version of that manager contemporary with the tag. Both runtime and package manager were digest-verified before use.

lockState.integrityNote: yarn lockfile v1 as written in 2017 carries no separate integrity field; the sha1 fragment on each resolved URL is the whole of its content addressing. sha512 SRI postdates this lockfile and is absent by construction, not by omission.
lockState.consequence: The closure IS pinned upstream, and every one of the 963 entries still resolved with its recorded sha1 in 2026.
lockState.packageManagerMismatch: The README offers `npm install` as an equal alternative, which would ignore yarn.lock entirely. Any work on this fixture must use yarn to keep the pin.

baseline.installDetail: yarn 1.3.2 materialised 1149 package directories from the committed lockfile in 19 seconds on Node 8.9.3, with --frozen-lockfile held and no lockfile write. Two unmet peer-dependency warnings from @angular/flex-layout, no deprecation warnings, no engine warnings.
baseline.buildDetail: Two production builds were attempted and both completed on the first try. `ng build --prod --aot` produced 524 files and 7828108 bytes in 44 seconds with a 1.48 MB main bundle and zero warnings. The repository's own `build-prod-en` chain — %BASE_HREF% substitution, AOT compile with the en XLIFF, ngsw-config, ngsw-worker copy, then substitution reversal — produced 526 files and 7938655 bytes in 48 seconds including ngsw.json and ngsw-worker.js, and the source file it mutates was verified restored.
baseline.significance: This fixture installs and builds clean as acquired, with no deviation, no pin repair and no workaround. No comparison against other fixtures in the corpus is made; this unit read none of their baselines.
baseline.unknownPreserved: Nothing observed here shows that the built application behaves correctly in a browser. No page was loaded and no journey was driven.

candidateJourneys: create a project from a translation file (/createproject — file input, FileReader, XLIFF/XMB parse, localStorage persist, workflow and role selection)
edit, translate and mark translation units (/translate — per-unit target editing, placeholder/tag warning dialog, translated versus final state by workflow type)
filter the unit list (/selectfilter — all, untranslated, needs-review, autotranslated, autotranslated-failed, autotranslated-ignored, plus substring search)
export the translated file (downloader service over file-saver; client-side download, never an upload)
manage projects: list, switch, edit, delete (/home, /editproject)
configure and run Google auto-translation (/configureautotranslate, /autotranslatesummary) — egress-bearing, out of the local-only closure

runtimeEgress.unconditional: https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon?family=Material+Icons — a stylesheet link in src/index.html, requested on every page load of every build variant. Blocked offline, the app still boots but every mat-icon renders as its ligature text instead of a glyph.
runtimeEgress.serviceWorkerCached: https://fonts.googleapis.com/** — the `fonts` assetGroup in src/ngsw-config.json, live only in the ngsw build variant
runtimeEgress.userInitiated: https://translation.googleapis.com/ — the optional auto-translate journey, which requires a user-supplied API key. No key ships with the fixture.
runtimeEgress.noBackend: There is no application server and no other host is contacted.

knownRisks: A TLS private key is committed at the repository root: cert.pem (1346 bytes) and key.pem (1708 bytes, a PEM PRIVATE KEY block), referenced by nothing in the build. The material is public upstream, must be treated as compromised, and must never be used or copied into a Versionless artifact.

The pin is a lightweight tag: no tag object, no tagger, no signature, and the commit is unsigned. Identity rests on the commit sha, the root tree sha and the archive digest. The upstream repository is not archived and was pushed as recently as 2022-12-07, so the ref could move.

Release-candidate and beta dependencies ship in this tagged release: @angular/material and @angular/cdk at 5.0.0-rc.2, @angular/flex-layout at 2.0.0-beta.10-4905443, the latter declaring Angular ~4.4.4 peers against the application's 5.0.3.

Two materially different production artifacts exist. A plain `ng build --prod` leaves the %BASE_HREF% placeholder un-substituted, so the bundle registers a service worker at the literal '%BASE_HREF%ngsw-worker.js' and ships no worker file; only the repository's build-prod-lang chain produces a coherent service-worker build. Any later witness must state which variant it drives, and the service-worker non-masking precedent applies to the ngsw variant.
The build-prod-lang chain rewrites src/environments/environment.prod.ts in place and reverses it afterwards. A failure between the two steps leaves the working tree mutated.

The application requests the Material Icons stylesheet from fonts.googleapis.com unconditionally. An offline witness will see every icon degrade to ligature text; that degradation must be declared, not masked.
The optional auto-translate journey contacts the Google Translate API with a user-supplied key. It is out of the local-only closure and must be blocked at witness time.
The README offers `npm install` as an alternative to yarn. Installing with npm would discard the committed lockfile and resolve 2017 ranges against today's registry.
